item.title: Palo Alto looks to rule on Churchill closure this spring
item.description: Spurred by recent deaths on the railroad tracks, Palo Alto officials announced Friday that they plan to make a decision on the closure of the Churchill Avenue crossing as soon as this spring, even as the city evaluates broader safety measures along the corridor. The post Palo Alto looks to rule on Churchill closure this spring appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: County supervisors take step toward saving allcove Palo Alto
item.description: The Santa Clara County Health and Hospital Committee recommended on Wednesday that the Board of Supervisors allocate $1.75 million to allcove Palo Alto over the next three years, underscoring community concerns about youth mental health and ongoing deaths by suicide. The post County supervisors take step toward saving allcove Palo Alto appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Superintendent Don Austin to leave Palo Alto Unified
item.description: The Palo Alto Board of Education and Superintendent Don Austin reached a mutual agreement to end his contract, effective immediately, in a closed session meeting on Friday morning. Austin, who joined the district in 2018, will assist the district with the transition until June 30. The post Superintendent Don Austin to leave Palo Alto Unified appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: San Mateo, Santa Clara counties top state’s priciest housing markets
item.description: While it became slightly easier to afford a home in California at the end of 2025, the state remains one of the nation’s toughest housing markets — especially in San Mateo and Santa Clara counties, which again ranked as the priciest places to buy a home.
